* We practice Collective Code Ownership so that anyone can change any line of code and anyone can introduce new libraries or tools.
* We deploy code on a regular basis, usually every day. IOW, we ship fast and learn fast. A typical recent week is around 45 pull requests merged.
* Claude Code and Codex do most of the typing. Engineers spend their time deciding what to build, writing the spec, and judging what comes back.
* We work one task per git worktree, which lets each of us keep several agent sessions running in parallel on isolated branches. Managing that parallelism is a skill in itself, and we will teach it.

* We invest heavily in the context our agents read: a repository-level conventions file, roughly two dozen project-specific skills, and purpose-built subagents. When someone learns something the hard way, it gets written down where the next agent will find it.

As an engineer on our team, you will help develop and deploy Raven—a powerful dynamic random test generator written in C++ that has been used extensively by CPU design teams throughout the Arm ecosystem for more than a decade. You will collaborate closely with senior CPU verification engineers both inside and outside Arm to understand their verification challenges and develop new ways of achieving their verification goals.
  
  
The Raven team is part of Arm’s Architecture & Technology Group, which develops architectural specifications and technologies that enable Arm’s partners to successfully develop processors conforming to the Arm architecture. In addition to supporting CPU verification teams, we collaborate early and frequently with Arm architects to help ensure that new architectural features can be verified effectively.
  
  
Your day-to-day work will consist primarily of developing our C++ verification technology and working directly with Raven users and verification teams to solve complex verification problems. This work relies heavily on a strong understanding of computer architecture and the ability to read, understand, and apply new architectural specifications.
  
  
If you are looking for a role that combines hardware and software skills, provides opportunities to work on challenging CPU verification problems, and allows you to make meaningful contributions to groundbreaking verification technologies and methodologies, we look forward to hearing from you.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Collaborate across the team to develop, document, test, and deploy Raven.
* Design and implement innovative Raven functionality to enable verification of architectural and microarchitectural features.
* Design and develop Raven test templates that exercise and stress architectural and microarchitectural features of Arm CPU designs.
* Investigate, debug, and resolve issues reported by Raven users and internal QA.
* Work directly with CPU verification engineers to understand verification challenges and develop effective solutions.
* Use AI responsibly to accelerate engineering work, while leading the resulting changes. * Professional software development experience in C++, with experience in Python or other scripting languages.
* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
* Strong software engineering skills, including knowledge of modern object-oriented programming, data structures, and algorithms.
* Experience with assembly-language programming and a strong understanding of computer architecture fundamentals, including concepts such as caches, TLBs, and processor pipelines.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Professional experience with microprocessor architecture, CPU verification, random test generation, or other complex software systems.

* Advanced CPU microarchitecture knowledge, including areas such as out-of-order execution, register renaming, and instruction scheduling.

* Experience collaborating across organizational and geographic boundaries.
